text:
Every Red Wings game this season comes with an asterisk named Dylan Larkin. He told the team he would no longer play for Detroit, and on October 29 the Red Wings suspended him without pay. Since then the story has run on two tracks: the trade rumors (the Wild, as The Athletic reported, are pushing hard; the Bruins have been linked; a recent headline says he has taken a hard stance on the list of teams he'd accept) and a team trying to prove it doesn't need him. On the ice, it mostly hasn't needed him. Alex DeBrincat has taken his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Viktor Arvidsson, Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the top power play, and Arvidsson has become the feel-good story of the fall, with a hat trick against Chicago and his 700th NHL game tonight. Finnie plays his 100th. "They've finally found it in Emmitt Finnie," Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom posted about Detroit's search for a top center, adding "(Only the slightest of hyperbole here)".

The play has held up better than the results. Detroit takes 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against), but its goal difference is -3 where the chances say +4.7: finishing has cost it 9.0 goals. Thursday summed it up, a 2-1 home loss to Vegas on Trevor Connelly's winner with 1:42 left. The other leak is in net. John Gibson has stopped .860 and sits at -6.3 goals saved above expected after +10.1 last season. If that's the real Gibson, Detroit is in trouble; we'd bet on last season being closer to the truth.

Colorado comes in a little bruised: a 3-2 overtime loss to Nashville on a Steven Stamkos winner, two nights after a 7-2 loss in Columbus, both right after three straight wins. Artturi Lehkonen is the hot hand, 11 points (8 goals) in his last ten, and it's earned: 5.3 expected goals on his own shots against 3.7 usual. Nathan MacKinnon is 85% for a point and 52% for two. Our sleeper is T.J. Hughes, 41% for a point on a line creating 4.10 expected goals per 60.

Our numbers have Colorado ahead, 3.28 expected goals to 2.87. For Detroit, every win without Larkin is an argument in the standoff: you can hold out, and we'll be fine.
headline: Detroit, playing on without Larkin

hunch.text: Detroit's finishing has to turn eventually, and our gut says it starts in Denver. Our numbers lean Colorado; our hunch is a Red Wings win.
